text.p: Bonds were slightly easier in line with the general trend, with market liquidity likely only to improve after the release of the U.S. durable goods figures.
The strength of the escudo was helping to underpin optimism of a rate cut by the Bank of Portugal in the near future.
Traders saw the decision of the Credit Institute to raise funds in yen under a swap deal as a further indication that the Bank of Portugal could be cutting rates soon.
"The Institute gave a signal that it does not agree with the level of interest rates in Portugal and the Bank of Portugal cannot completely ignore it," said one trader.
But traders saw little scope for any further immediate narrowing in the 10-year cash spread with the Bunds.

On the other hand, even if the U.S. numbers provoked fresh concerns of a rate rise there, the approach of the end of the month was likely to restrict the scope for selling of Portuguese bonds, they added.
